newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay sees modest rise in 1997 ATKs.
newsitem.headline: Cathay sees modest rise in 1997 ATKs.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd is projecting a 2.8 percent rise in available tonne kilometres (ATKs) for cargo in 1997 and a 4.5 percent rise in overall route network ATKs, the Hong Kong carrier's 1996 annual report said.
Analysts said the report held few surprises and the ATK forecast was "low" and "modest but realistic" considering capacity constraints at Cathay's congested home airport at Kai Tak.
ATK stands for the average tonne per km and refers to capacity.

"Obviously Cathay does not have the landing capacity because Kai Tak has been squeezed about as far as it can go so it doesn't surprise me that they expect growth to be low compared to recent years," said Peter Negline, senior research analyst at Salomon Brothers.

"These numbers indicate that the new airport (Chek Lap Kok) is coming on stream just at the right time and it is a positive sign that Cathay have been able to match that with when they will take delivery of more new aircraft - their planning seems just right. I am also quite impressed with the increases in aircraft utilisation which shows Cathay are able to operate their business very efficiently," he added.

Another analyst said the ATK projections were "fairly low" considering the average per annum ATK growth over the past 5 years had been 12.3 per cent. He also attributed 1997's lower forecasts to the restriction in capacity until Hong Kong's new airport opens and when Cathay's next batch of new aircraft are due to arrive.
Cost per ATK in 1996 fell by 5 percent because of better operational efficiencies, the annual report said

On Cathay's cargo operations, the report said industry wide downward trends in yields continued to put pressure on revenues, despite relatively high load factors. Charges were raised to try and maintain yields but with only limited success, while freighter crews sourced from subsidiary recruitment company Aircrew Services Ltd have resulted in greater operational efficiencies, the report said.

Cargo and mail accounted for HK$6.97 billion turnover out of a total of HK$32.38 billion, while cargo tonnes rose to 568,147 tonnes from 531,339 tonnes. Cargo and mail load factors dropped marginally to 66.9 per cent from to 67 percent but cargo yield fell by 7.2 percent, the report said.

Utilisation rates of Cathay Cargo's seven Boeing 747-200 freighters was unchanged at 13.8 hours but utilisation of the company's two Boeing 747-400 freighters rose from 14.7 hours in 1995 to 15.2 hours last year. Overall aircraft utilisation rates rose 5.6 percent to 11.4 percent.

Cathay also said its fuel hedging policy had partly mitigated the effect of the fuel price hike resulting in 6.4 percent savings in average gross fuel costs. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
